REBECCA WEBBER tells of the questions which came to her mind as she looked from the window of a speeding train at the various types of electrical structures which came into view.

brief_context: Mentioned in a newspaper headline about electricity pylons.
brief_extract:
The answers which she subsequently found may interest other readers

OUTWARD bound on a long railway journey, my thoughts were turned to electricity, first by the various structures seen as we were carried through the countryside, and then by a discussion which was taking place among other occupants of the carriage. As we passed poles, steel towers and masts extending long fingers into the sky or making an almost lacy pattern against a green or blue background, I wondered how much there was in the protesting column in the morning paper, "Pylons across Hadrian's Wall," or in the objections to the erection of electricity supply lines in Lakeland. As scraps of the conversation came across to me I began to take a new interest in the shapes in steel, brick or concrete which came into our line of vision and receded again as we flashed in and out of villages, through great towns and across stretches of countryside.

brief_context: Place where Mrs. Lawson worked before her marriage.
brief_extract: Mrs. Lawson is one of the many women who today combine a full-time job with running a home, for she is responsible for the well-being of two sons, one still a schoolboy, as well as "Rex." Until her marriage she worked in the office of an engineering and shipbuilding firm on Tyneside and is therefore a real "Geordie." Her husband was a marine engineer who, during his travels round the world, collected for her some beautiful specimens of Eastern craftsmanship which enable her to travel in mind in "the realms of gold." A treasured memory, too, is Queen Mary's interest in her family affairs during Her Majesty's visit to the E.A.W. Headquarters.

AFTER telling my friends that I had travelled nearly 40,000 miles during three months whilst visiting the United States of America in Autumn, 1951, I felt they would get the impression that I had merely taken a passing glance at a large number of places and cities, always harassed by the thought of a travelling "time table." In these days, however, with a little thoughtful planning it is quite possible to stay long enough at a large number of places to study almost leisurely the way of life of people and to come into intimate contact with the various groups of society. I sailed from Liverpool to New York and passed a most interest- ing three weeks at Washington visiting the Senate and Congress Committee Sessions, and meeting a fascinating array of famous State Department personalities.

brief_context: Used as a comparison for appliance usage and food economy.
brief_extract: I therefore took into account the income range of the household when studying American homes and saw with considerable pleasure the excellent equipment and— what is more—equipment which is really used and not merely purchased for ornament. Cookers, kettles, irons, washing machines, kitchen mixers were commonplace in many houses where the husband would be described over here as a "manual worker." Refrigerators were not quite so obvious but were certainly very much in evidence—much more so than in England. In the slightly higher income groups the very successful food freezers were a joy to behold, and I believe that it is in this field that our manufacturers could contribute a great deal to food economy in England by the production of comparable units.

brief_context: Electricity unit cost is similar to that in Great Britain.
brief_extract:
Tariffs

There are many hundreds of electrical enterprises and nearly a thousand different tariffs, though a national block tariff is under consideration. The price of electricity is unchanged since 1936, the unit cost is similar to that in Great Britain, but as wages and salaries are higher the percentage of income spent on electricity is lower. Five cents are equivalent to 1d., and an average rate for cooking is 6 1/2 cents, water heating 3.4 cents, small appliances 10.4 cents, lighting 33.1 cents, with an average of 8.95 cents for general domestic purposes.

Testing

All electrical apparatus, large and small, flex, plugs and sockets, switches, connectors, cable, lamps, meters, etc., bear the letters ASEV as such or in Morse code to indicate technical quality, safety and durability. brief_context: Swiss town where hire purchase and housing were discussed.
brief_extract: Half the municipal flats in Zurich have electric cookers, and in the City's new housing estates there are no gas mains; all flats have a cooker and water-heater, and the more expensive ones have refrigeration facilities, the appliances belonging to the flat and not to the tenant. Hire purchase terms are seldom available except for refrigerators, and the only example met by Miss Piattt was in Lausanne, a town with 35,000 households, more than half cooking by electricity, and where the cheapest unit charge in the country obtained. Here a cooker, washing machine, refrigerator or water heater was available by a 20% deposit, the total charge being increased by one-quarter.

brief_context: Location of showrooms with a 24-hour light bulb machine.
brief_extract: A repairs service is established in the Zurich Showrooms, the rental of municipal and other flats includes repair work unless the fault is due to bad treatment. A very practical consumer service outside the Berne Showrooms was an automatic machine containing electric light bulbs of a variety of wattages, fuses and connectors available during non-business hours. In Lausanne the town does not build flats, but will often give a building site and pay up to 40% of the total cost.

brief_context: Region with compulsory housecraft instruction for young women.
brief_extract: There was a demand for housecraft schools and in 1933 a law made such instruction compulsory for every girl between the age of 16 and 20, and is in force in half the Cantons. In the Canton of Zurich attendance for 320 hours is obligatory unless marriage immediately follows school. There are several courses available and the girl from factory, shop, office or household can take the course at set periods during the working week; the girl of 15 can take a final year's general course including housecraft training; while a 6-months college course is frequently taken on leaving High School.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding its grandeur and architecture.
brief_extract:
Land of Contrasts

Italy is indeed a land of contrasts, where the sudden disruption of life by flood or volcano is counterbalanced by the age-long tradition of beauty apparent on every hand, and by the continuity with a past of nearly thirty centuries. The “grandeur that was Rome” is linked to the richness of mediæval Florence, and in the echoes of La Scala Opera House at Milan one recalls all the dukes of this proud city, both in and outside the pages of Shakespeare. In the Bay of Naples a moment of 1st-century time with its high civilisation is preserved at Pompeii, while the many villas on the orange-clad slopes rising steep from the sea are reminders of their occupancy by poets and artists of all ages, from the 16th century to the Victorian Age.

article_title: TO THE TOWN HALL AT SCARBOROUGH
brief_extract: We were privileged to witness an episode in the town's modern history when the Mayor presented awards, on behalf of the Royal Humane Society and the R.S.P.C.A. The first was for the rescue of a dog from the sea, the second for rescuing a little girl from drowning in the harbour, and the third for rescuing another dog from the Castle Cliff, where it had been marooned for two days. Delegates to the 27th Annual Conference at Scarborough will be able to join us in adding to the history of the town.

article_title: A GRAPHIC DESCRIPTION OF WATER SUPPLY OLD AND NEW
brief_extract:
B. Shaw, Newcastle (Staffs) Branch

IT was amazing to hear that less than 100 years ago water was purchased at a halfpenny a pailful, that drinking water in places was so scarce as to be bought by the farthingsworth, that potatoes were boiled in water that lay in the fields, a yellowish fluid possibly having been pumped out of the ironstone mines. Scrubbing water had to be carried from canals and pools.

brief_context: An old source of water compared to modern machinery.
article_title: A GRAPHIC DESCRIPTION OF WATER SUPPLY OLD AND NEW
brief_extract: Scrubbing water had to be carried from canals and pools. One compares the then Public Pump and Spring Wells with the gleaming machinery used in the modern pumping stations all over the country. The vast piping system that brings pure water to our homes may be contrasted with an old wooden water pipe discovered during excavations, which had been made from a hollowed-out tree trunk and laid in Newcastle at the end of the 18th century.

They were the first visitors to the new North Tees "C" Power Station, built to keep pace with the growing demands for electricity on the North-East Coast, and the third station on the site. The visit was one of contrasts, for the gay flowers at the entrance and the expanse of soil later to receive green turf threw into relief the smoke and medley of cranes and chimneys on the far side of the river.

brief_context: Location where courses for teachers have been run.
brief_extract:
Teachers
More and more teachers are including some form of electrical education in the curriculum, and they ask for local Refresher Courses dealing with their special difficulties and local peculiarities, such as hard water and its effect on electric water heaters, and the particular apparatus installed in the schools in the town. Courses have been run in Leicester, Birmingham, Walsall and Coventry, and in the counties of Derby, Salop, and Worcester. In all these various courses the most interesting outcome has been the questions asked, e.g., "Why should school cookers be so large and different from those used in homes, thus making teachers' work so much more difficult?" The result is that today the cookers in Domestic Science Centres are gradually being replaced by the ordinary domestic size as used in the homes in that locality.

brief_context: Country where the factory and farming centres are located.
article_title: TO SCOTT’S PORAGE OATS FACTORY, CUPAR
brief_extract: They described the various stages of processing and packing this renowned cereal, all of which are carried out by electrical machinery, and from the raw material to the enclosed package the cereal is entirely untouched by hand. The factory is ideally situated in the heart of the pleasant countryside near Cupar, one of Scotland’s most important farming centres, so that much of the oats used is actually grown locally. Inside the factory one is immediately impressed by the cleanliness and efficiency prevailing.

brief_context: Origin of the packing machine at the factory.
article_title: TO SCOTT’S PORAGE OATS FACTORY, CUPAR
brief_extract: It is the aim of the management never to retain the oats in the factory for more than three days to ensure their freshness on reaching shops. Members were pleased to hear that all the machinery, with the exception of the American packing machine, was made in the Lothians, near Edinburgh. The refreshments which rounded off the visit came straight from the baking machines and included oat-cakes and shortbread “fancies” made by the firm.

brief_context: Beach location for a New England clambake.
brief_extract:
Meals
Any traveller is interested in
meals, but to attend three ban-
quets of three different clubs in
one evening is a formidable
undertaking! Perhaps the most
outstanding gastronomic recol-
lections are of a real New Eng-
land "clambake" on the beach
at Plymouth, and a "barbecue,"
again in the open air, at Santa
Barbara, California, amid the
brilliant flowers and old Spanish
architecture, and followed by an
earthquake at night-the worst
there since 1925. In Texas I was
intrigued to learn that notices ad-
vertising "chicken in the rough"
meant quite literally a rough-and-
ready way of eating cooked
chicken.

a wealth of interest in scenic
beauty and in animal interest.

brief_extract:
modern conditions there is no practical alternative to the general provision of light, radio and small power through the low tension distribution systems, and that the provision in addition of capacity to meet the needs for cooking, water heating and comfort heating is in the nature of an incremental capital cost only."

It is a significant reflection that any curtailment of domestic supply would result in dearer electricity for industry. Atmospheric Pollution
"The pollution of the atmosphere by smoke, dust and noxious vapour is of particular significance in the national economy of such a densely populated island as Great Britain, and the consequences are enhanced by our geographical position, which leads to relatively low prevailing wind velocities as compared with some other countries of the world. Great Britain in the past was notorious for its fogs, and credit is seldom given to the electricity supply industry for the benefits conferred by the substantial reduction in fog prevalence and severity which has been obtained through the years by the substitution of efficient combustion in power stations for far less efficient combustion in factory and dwelling house."

Today the domestic chimney is probably still responsible for nearly half the total cost of pollution put conservatively at about £95 million.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding a survey about television and launderers.
brief_extract: THE advent of television marked a further milestone in the history of electronics, and, like the coming of sound broadcasting, it has already made a very considerable change in our domestic habits. In America, for example, a recent survey shows that launderers there lament a very serious decline in the number of their dress-shirt clients, who now sit at home with eyes glued to their television screens. During my lifetime I, like many others, have seen (or heard) the start of several of the things which have now become commonplace.

brief_extract:
The National Register of Electrical Installation
Contractors established over 26 years ago,
aims at maintaining a high standard of quali-
fication and raising the efficiency and status of
Electrical Installation Contractors, thereby safe-
guarding the public against inferior materials
and workmanship. The National Register of Electrical Installation
Contractors is an independent body directed by
representatives of important Associations inter-
ested in electrical installation work, including
The Institution of Electrical Engineers, The
Association of Consulting Engineers, The Elec-
trical Contractors' Association of Scotland, The
Royal Institute of British Architects, The Elec-
trical Association for Women, The National
Farmers' Union. Electrical Installation Contractors holding the
Certificate of the National Register have given
evidence of competency; their work is subject
to periodical inspection; they undertake to pay
rates of wages and observe conditions of em-
ployment not less favourable than those of the
appropriate trade agreement; and observe the
Regulations for the Electrical Equipment of
Buildings issued by the Institution of Electrical
Engineers.

article_title: TO THE EMPIRE CARPET MANUFACTURING CO. LTD. KIDDERMINSTER
brief_extract:
Newton, Hon. Secretary, Wellington, Shropshire
THE making of carpets was seen, from
the design to the finished article, in-
cluding inspection of the undyed
wool, the dyeing and drying sheds,
where old and new methods are used,
the beaming and sizing sections, the
weaving on machines, some of which
take up to two weeks to set up, the
stockrooms stacked with bundles of
wool in exquisite shades ready for
weaving, the overlooking and finishing
departments, where girls worked at
lightning speed, and the stockrooms
of finished goods. Of special interest was an electronic
"brain" which controls and operates
one of the biggest single advances
ever made in the warp sizing and
beaming sections of the industry.

ables the operator to select a winding
speed of from one to ten yards a

yards a minute on the old process. This control mechanism is the result
of years of work by engineers of
British Electronic Products Ltd., of
Rugeley, Staffs, and manufactured by
Sellers & Co. Ltd., Huddersfield.

article_title: VISIT TO CALIFORNIA — LAND OF SUNSHINE
brief_extract: One has to be actually among the tall, thin buildings to realise just how small one is and how vast are the concrete and steel structures. From the top of the Empire State Building I looked down from 1,000 feet above the roadways to where as far as the eye could see towards the north are the ordered modern buildings and wide roads criss-crossing one another, and to the south where the modern city has grown from the older part. On the east and west the city stretches down to the waters of the East and Hudson Rivers respectively.

article_title: VISIT TO CALIFORNIA — LAND OF SUNSHINE
brief_extract: I was impressed with the grandeur of the scenery: the vast open spaces and the great mountain range. I felt a little nervous when passing through some of the desert parts, in particular Death Valley, where both the lowest and highest points in America are to be found in close proximity. The range of colours is immensely beautiful and the stillness of the region is almost uncanny.

brief_context: The coastal region reached after the cross-country trip.

brief_extract: The range of colours is immensely beautiful and the stillness of the region is almost uncanny. As I reached the West Coast I travelled through lime and orange groves which stretched for miles in all directions, merging with the horizon and looking like a glorious carpet of gold and green. In contrast I saw the oilfields of Western America.

article_title: VISIT TO CALIFORNIA — LAND OF SUNSHINE
brief_extract:
Winifred V. Willis, Woolwich

I FLEW from Heathrow via Iceland to New York, where I went for a coach tour. One has to be actually among the tall, thin buildings to realise just how small one is and how vast are the concrete and steel structures.

brief_context: Comparing electrical appliance familiarity between American and British kitchens.
brief_extract: Electrical appliances, such as coffee percolators, mixers, toasters, cleaners and irons, are to be found in nearly every kitchen. The electric cooker has many refinements not universally familiar in Britain. In addition to the normal grill and hotplates, the cooker has two ovens, one smaller than the other, which enables two dishes requiring different temperatures to be prepared at the same time.

brief_context: Comparing the individuality of British homes to Californian ones.
brief_extract: My daughter has a portable set which can be moved to some of the rooms which have a specially fitted window. Gay colours predominate in Californian homes, but the furnishings lack the individuality of British homes. The “self-service” system in the large stores is a convenience.

brief_context: Describing the predominant colours and furnishings in homes there.
brief_extract: grime to many larger cities of the world, the houses are clean and bright, mostly whitewashed, with brick-red tiled roofs, with flowers, many semi-tropical, growing in gardens all the year round. Californians love the outdoor life, and in summer many families eat a lot of meals in their garden patios with barbecue fires, serving one hot main course with salads and relishes, and ice cream for dessert. In my daughter’s home I examined the electrical aids which are regarded by the average American housewife to be the normal if not essential accou-trements which go to make the American way of life what it is today.
